title: Grade 4 Science — Wed, May 20
description: Food & Nutrition — Day 3 of 5: Digestion and how food is processed
subject: science

questions.question: Digestion begins in the:
questions.explanation: Digestion starts in the mouth — chewing breaks food mechanically, and saliva begins chemical digestion of starch.

questions.question: What is the role of the stomach in digestion?
options: Churns food and breaks it down with acid and enzymes
Pushes digested food out of the body
questions.explanation: The stomach churns food and uses gastric acid and enzymes to break down proteins and kill bacteria.

questions.question: Where is most of the absorption of nutrients into blood?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is where most digested food (glucose, amino acids, fatty acids) is absorbed into the bloodstream.

questions.question: The large intestine mainly:
options: Absorbs water and forms solid waste
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested food, forming solid waste (faeces) for elimination.

questions.question: Saliva in the mouth contains which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Saliva contains amylase — it breaks down starch into simpler sugars. Bread tastes slightly sweet after chewing because of this!

questions.question: What does bile do?
options: Breaks up fats into tiny droplets for digestion
questions.explanation: Bile (made in the liver, stored in gallbladder) emulsifies fats — breaks them into tiny droplets so enzymes can digest them.

questions.question: The correct order of digestion is:
options: Mouth → Small intestine → Stomach → Large intestine
Mouth → Stomach → Small intestine → Large intestine
Stomach → Mouth → Large intestine → Small intestine
Mouth → Large intestine → Small intestine → Stomach
questions.explanation: Mouth (chew/saliva) → Stomach (acid+enzymes) → Small intestine (absorption) → Large intestine (water) → Excretion.

questions.question: Teeth are important for digestion because:
options: They mechanically break food into smaller pieces for easier chemical digestion
questions.explanation: Teeth grind and chew food into smaller pieces, increasing surface area for enzymes to work on.

questions.question: Why should you chew food slowly and thoroughly?
options: To give saliva time to start digestion and break food into smaller pieces
To make the meal last longer
It doesn't matter how you chew
questions.explanation: Thorough chewing breaks food into smaller pieces, mixes it with saliva, and starts starch digestion — making later digestion easier.

questions.question: The tube connecting the mouth to the stomach is called the:
questions.explanation: The oesophagus (food pipe) carries food from the mouth to the stomach by muscular contractions.

questions.question: Which organ produces digestive enzymes AND insulin?
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces digestive enzymes (for fats, proteins, carbs) AND insulin (to control blood sugar).

questions.question: What is the function of the liver in digestion?
questions.explanation: The liver: (1) produces bile for fat digestion, (2) processes and detoxifies absorbed nutrients, (3) stores glycogen.

questions.question: Drinking water helps digestion because:
options: Water makes food softer, helps dissolve nutrients, and carries them through the body
Water has no role in digestion
questions.explanation: Water softens food, dissolves nutrients, and helps move food through the digestive tract. Dehydration causes constipation.

questions.question: Which part of the gut is the longest?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is about 6–7 metres long — longer than the large intestine! It has a huge surface area for absorption.

questions.question: What happens to waste that cannot be digested?
options: It goes back to the stomach
It is sent to the lungs
It passes to the large intestine and is excreted as faeces
It stays in the small intestine forever
questions.explanation: Indigestible material (mainly fibre) passes to the large intestine where water is absorbed, and the rest is excreted.
